questions.explanation: Fixed terms and for-cause removal protection insulate commissions such as the SEC and FCC from at-will presidential removal. The scope of that protection has been narrowed by recent decisions but remains the defining structural feature.

questions.stem: The Bay of Pigs invasion (1961) was an attempt to:
choices: Remove Fidel Castro using Cuban exile forces
Blockade Soviet shipping to Cuba
Install missiles in Turkey
Support a coup in the Dominican Republic
questions.explanation: The CIA-organized exile landing failed within days and damaged the new Kennedy administration's credibility. The naval quarantine of Cuba came the following year during the missile crisis.

questions.stem: The Church Committee (1975-76) is remembered for:
choices: Investigating intelligence agency abuses and prompting new oversight structures
Drafting the War Powers Resolution
Impeachment proceedings against President Nixon
Reforming the federal budget process
questions.explanation: Its findings on domestic surveillance, assassination plots, and covert action led to permanent intelligence committees in both chambers and to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It is the origin of the modern intelligence oversight framework.

questions.stem: NAFTA, in force from 1994, created a free trade area among:
choices: The United States, Canada, and Mexico
The United States and the European Union
All countries of the Western Hemisphere
The United States, Mexico, and Central America
questions.explanation: NAFTA linked the three North American economies and was replaced by the USMCA in 2020. The fourth option describes CAFTA-DR, a separate agreement with Central America and the Dominican Republic.

questions.stem: The Antideficiency Act prohibits federal officials from:
choices: Obligating funds in excess of available appropriations
Accepting gifts from foreign governments
Lobbying Congress on pending legislation
Disclosing classified information
questions.explanation: The Act bars spending or committing money before it is appropriated, and it is the legal reason agencies must shut down non-excepted activities during a funding lapse. Violations carry administrative and potentially criminal penalties.

questions.stem: The Emoluments Clauses of the Constitution concern:
choices: Acceptance of payments or gifts from foreign states by federal officeholders
Congressional pay raises
Presidential pardons
Compensation of federal judges
questions.explanation: The Foreign Emoluments Clause bars officeholders from accepting presents or emoluments from foreign states without congressional consent, and a separate Domestic Emoluments Clause fixes the President's compensation. Judicial salary protection is in Article III.

questions.stem: The Smith-Mundt Act, as amended, principally governs:
choices: The dissemination of U.S. government international broadcasting and public diplomacy material
Export controls on defense articles
Security clearances for federal employees
Foreign lobbying registration
questions.explanation: Smith-Mundt authorizes public diplomacy and international broadcasting and long restricted domestic dissemination of that material, a restriction relaxed in 2013. Foreign lobbying is covered by FARA, and export controls by the Arms Export Control Act.

questions.stem: Which best describes the relationship between the Secretary of State and the Foreign Service?
choices: The Secretary is the President's principal foreign policy adviser and heads the Department in which the Foreign Service serves
The Secretary commands Foreign Service officers as military officers are commanded
The Foreign Service reports to the National Security Adviser
The Secretary is elected by senior Foreign Service officers
questions.explanation: The Secretary leads the Department of State and is the President's principal adviser on foreign affairs. The National Security Adviser coordinates interagency policy but has no line authority over the Department.

questions.stem: The dissent channel at the Department of State exists to:
choices: Allow employees to register policy disagreement without retaliation
Permit anonymous reporting of criminal misconduct
Appeal performance evaluations
Challenge security clearance denials
questions.explanation: Created after Vietnam, the dissent channel provides a protected route for policy disagreement that reaches senior leadership directly. Misconduct reporting runs through the Inspector General, a separate mechanism with different protections.

questions.stem: The Thirty Years' War (1618-48) was fought primarily in:
choices: The Iberian Peninsula
Central Europe, especially the German lands
The Balkans
The Low Countries only
questions.explanation: The war devastated the German lands of the Holy Roman Empire, with population losses in some regions approaching a third. It ended at Westphalia, whose settlement is conventionally treated as the origin of the sovereign state system.

questions.stem: The Meiji Restoration and the Self-Strengthening Movement are best compared as:
choices: Two successful modernization programs in Japan and China respectively
Modernization efforts of which Japan's succeeded far more thoroughly than China's
Two failed attempts to resist Western influence
Programs that both led to constitutional monarchy
questions.explanation: Both responded to Western pressure, but Japan achieved comprehensive institutional transformation while Qing reform remained partial and was checked by court politics. The divergence is a standard case study in why similar external pressures produce different outcomes.

questions.stem: Which is the world's longest river system?
choices: The Amazon
The Nile
The Yangtze
The Mississippi
questions.explanation: The Nile is conventionally listed as longest at roughly 6,650 km, though the Amazon carries far more water and some measurements place it longer depending on which headwaters are counted. The Amazon is unambiguously the largest by discharge.

questions.stem: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848):
choices: Ended the Mexican-American War and transferred roughly half of Mexico's territory to the United States
Established the Gadsden Purchase boundary
Settled the Oregon boundary with Britain
Recognized Texas independence
questions.explanation: The treaty ceded present-day California, Nevada, Utah, and parts of several other states. The Gadsden Purchase came five years later, and the Oregon question was settled with Britain in 1846 by separate agreement.

questions.stem: Which country has the largest Muslim population?
choices: Saudi Arabia
Indonesia
Egypt
Iran
questions.explanation: Indonesia has roughly 230 million Muslims, far more than any Arab state. The assumption that the Muslim world is centered on the Middle East is a persistent error — South and Southeast Asia together hold the majority.

questions.stem: The Peace of Utrecht (1713) is significant for:
choices: Ending the War of the Spanish Succession and articulating the balance of power principle
Concluding the Seven Years' War
Partitioning Poland
Ending the Napoleonic Wars
questions.explanation: Utrecht separated the French and Spanish crowns and explicitly invoked equilibrium among the powers — the first major treaty to state balance of power as a governing principle. The Seven Years' War ended at Paris in 1763.

questions.stem: The Strait of Gibraltar separates:
choices: Europe from Africa, connecting the Atlantic to the Mediterranean
The Black Sea from the Aegean
The Red Sea from the Indian Ocean
The Baltic from the North Sea
questions.explanation: Gibraltar is the western entrance to the Mediterranean, roughly 13 km wide at its narrowest. The other options describe the Turkish Straits, Bab-el-Mandeb, and the Danish Straits respectively.

questions.stem: The Congress of Berlin (1878) principally addressed:
choices: The partition of Africa
The reorganization of the Balkans after the Russo-Turkish War
German unification
The Moroccan crisis
questions.explanation: Bismarck's Congress revised the Treaty of San Stefano, curbing Russian gains and reshaping Balkan borders in ways that stored up the grievances feeding later crises. The Berlin Conference on Africa is a separate meeting in 1884-85.

questions.stem: Which country lies directly between Poland and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave and Belarus, forming the Suwałki Gap?
choices: Latvia
Lithuania
Estonia
Ukraine
questions.explanation: The Suwałki Gap is the narrow Polish-Lithuanian border corridor between Kaliningrad and Belarus. It is treated as a critical vulnerability in NATO planning because it is the only land link to the Baltic states.

questions.stem: The Green Revolution of the mid-twentieth century refers to:
choices: The rise of environmental political parties
The spread of high-yield crop varieties, fertilizers, and irrigation that sharply raised agricultural output
Decolonization in sub-Saharan Africa
The 1979 Iranian Revolution
questions.explanation: Associated with Norman Borlaug, it dramatically increased yields in Mexico, India, and elsewhere, averting predicted famines. Its ecological costs and uneven distribution of benefits remain subjects of serious debate.

questions.stem: The African Union succeeded which earlier body?
choices: The Non-Aligned Movement
The Organization of African Unity
The Economic Community of West African States
The Southern African Development Community
questions.explanation: The AU replaced the OAU in 2002, adopting a mandate that permits intervention in member states in grave circumstances — a significant departure from the OAU's strict non-interference norm. ECOWAS and SADC are subregional bodies that continue to exist.

questions.stem: The Treaty of Portsmouth (1905), mediated by Theodore Roosevelt, ended:
choices: The Boxer Rebellion
The Russo-Japanese War
The First Sino-Japanese War
The Boer War
questions.explanation: Roosevelt's mediation earned him the Nobel Peace Prize and marked the first time an Asian power defeated a European one in modern war. The First Sino-Japanese War ended at Shimonoseki in 1895.

questions.stem: Which of these countries does NOT border the Mediterranean Sea?
choices: Algeria
Portugal
Lebanon
Croatia
questions.explanation: Portugal's coastline faces only the Atlantic. Spain sits between Portugal and the Mediterranean, which is what makes the distractor plausible for anyone picturing Iberia as a single Mediterranean unit.

questions.stem: The Sykes-Picot Agreement and the Balfour Declaration are frequently discussed together because:
choices: Both were negotiated at the Paris Peace Conference
Both were British wartime commitments concerning Ottoman territory that proved difficult to reconcile
Both were repudiated before the war ended
Both were ratified by the League of Nations
questions.explanation: Britain made overlapping commitments to France, to Arab leaders, and to the Zionist movement within roughly two years. The tension among them shaped the mandate period and the region's subsequent conflicts.

questions.stem: Which mountain range runs along the western edge of South America?
choices: The Rockies
The Andes
The Atlas
The Urals
questions.explanation: The Andes extend roughly 7,000 km along the Pacific coast, the longest continental mountain range in the world. The Atlas range is in northwest Africa and the Urals divide European from Asian Russia.

questions.stem: The Warsaw Pact was dissolved in:
questions.explanation: The Pact was formally dissolved in July 1991, months before the Soviet Union itself. 1989 saw the revolutions in Eastern Europe that made the alliance unsustainable, which is why that year is the common wrong answer.

questions.stem: The Sahel, the Maghreb, and the Horn of Africa are all:
choices: Political unions of African states
Regional designations within Africa
Colonial-era administrative districts
River basins
questions.explanation: All three are geographic regions: the semi-arid belt south of the Sahara, the northwest African coastal region, and the northeast African peninsula. None corresponds to a formal political organization.

questions.stem: The Bretton Woods system collapsed primarily because:
choices: Member states withdrew from the IMF
The United States suspended dollar convertibility into gold in 1971
The Soviet Union joined the system
European currencies were devalued in 1949
questions.explanation: Mounting dollar liabilities against a fixed gold stock made convertibility unsustainable, and Nixon's suspension ended the fixed-rate regime. The IMF survived and adapted to a floating-rate world rather than dissolving with the system it was built to manage.

questions.stem: Which body of water separates Australia from New Zealand?
choices: The Coral Sea
The Tasman Sea
The Timor Sea
The Arafura Sea
questions.explanation: The Tasman Sea lies between the two, roughly 2,000 km wide. The Timor and Arafura Seas lie to Australia's north toward Indonesia, and the Coral Sea to its northeast.

questions.stem: The Cuban Missile Crisis was resolved in part by an undisclosed American commitment to:
choices: Recognize the Castro government
Withdraw Jupiter missiles from Turkey
End the trade embargo on Cuba
Withdraw forces from Berlin
questions.explanation: Alongside the public pledge not to invade Cuba, Kennedy privately agreed to remove the Turkish missiles — a concession kept secret for years so as not to appear to reward Soviet pressure. The embargo remained in place.

questions.stem: Deflation is generally considered dangerous because it:
choices: Raises the real burden of existing debt and can encourage consumers to postpone purchases
Always accompanies rapid growth
Reduces the value of savings
Forces central banks to raise interest rates
questions.explanation: Falling prices increase the real value of fixed debts and give buyers reason to wait, weakening demand further. Japan's experience after 1990 is the standard cautionary case for why central banks target modest positive inflation rather than zero.

questions.stem: The Phillips curve originally described a relationship between:
choices: Interest rates and investment
Unemployment and inflation
Trade deficits and exchange rates
Money supply and output
questions.explanation: The curve posited an inverse relationship between unemployment and inflation. The 1970s stagflation undermined the simple version, and modern formulations incorporate expectations, which is why the relationship is treated as short-run at best.

questions.stem: A subsidy on domestic production has an effect on trade that is most similar to:
choices: A tariff on imports
An export tax
A floating exchange rate
A capital control
questions.explanation: Both advantage domestic producers over foreign competitors, though a subsidy is paid by taxpayers while a tariff is paid by purchasers. This equivalence is why trade agreements discipline subsidies alongside tariffs.

questions.stem: Anti-dumping duties are imposed when a country determines that imports are:
choices: Sold below normal value, causing injury to a domestic industry
Produced with subsidized inputs
Of substandard quality
Entering in quantities above a negotiated quota
questions.explanation: Dumping means selling in an export market below home-market price or below cost, with material injury required for duties. Subsidized inputs are addressed by countervailing duties, a parallel but distinct remedy.

questions.stem: The velocity of money refers to:
choices: The rate at which the money supply grows
The average number of times a unit of currency is used in transactions over a period
The speed of electronic payments
The rate at which currency depreciates
questions.explanation: Velocity is the turnover rate of money and appears in the quantity equation MV = PQ. A decline in velocity can offset monetary expansion, which is one reason large increases in the money supply do not always produce proportional inflation.

questions.stem: A sovereign debt restructuring typically involves:
choices: Immediate repayment in full
Reducing the face value, extending maturities, or lowering interest on outstanding debt
Transferring the debt to the IMF
Converting debt to equity in state enterprises
questions.explanation: Restructuring changes the terms — a haircut, longer maturities, or lower coupons — through negotiation with creditors. Collective action clauses now facilitate the process by binding holdout creditors to a supermajority agreement.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a trade quota?
choices: A tax on imported goods
A quantitative limit on the amount of a good that may be imported
A ban on all trade with a country
A minimum price for imported goods
questions.explanation: A quota restricts quantity directly rather than raising price through taxation. Quotas tend to be less transparent than tariffs and generate rents for whoever holds the import licenses rather than revenue for the government.

questions.stem: The Lewis model of development describes growth driven by:
choices: Transfer of surplus labor from a traditional agricultural sector to a modern industrial sector
Import substitution behind tariff walls
Foreign aid financing infrastructure
Rising commodity prices
questions.explanation: Arthur Lewis described a dual economy in which industrial expansion draws on effectively unlimited rural labor until a turning point is reached. It remains a reference point in analyses of Chinese and other East Asian industrialization.

questions.stem: A recession is conventionally identified by:
choices: Any quarter of negative growth
A significant, broad-based decline in economic activity lasting more than a few months
Unemployment above 10 percent
A fall in the stock market of 20 percent or more
questions.explanation: The common two-consecutive-quarters rule of thumb is not the formal criterion; official dating considers depth, diffusion, and duration across multiple indicators. A 20 percent equity decline defines a bear market, not a recession.

questions.stem: Financial contagion refers to:
choices: The transmission of a crisis from one country or market to others
The spread of counterfeit currency
Rapid inflation in neighboring economies
Coordinated central bank intervention
questions.explanation: Contagion may run through trade links, common creditors, or shifts in investor sentiment that treat dissimilar economies as a class. The 1997 Asian crisis and its spread to Russia and Brazil is the canonical illustration.

questions.stem: Which is the best example of an intangible barrier to trade?
choices: A 15 percent tariff
Divergent product safety standards that imported goods must separately satisfy
An import quota
A currency peg
questions.explanation: Non-tariff barriers such as standards, licensing, and customs procedures can restrict trade as effectively as duties while being harder to measure and negotiate. Much modern trade diplomacy concerns them rather than tariffs.

questions.stem: The J-curve effect describes how a currency depreciation initially:
choices: Improves the trade balance immediately
Worsens the trade balance before improving it as volumes adjust
Has no effect on trade
Raises domestic interest rates
questions.explanation: Prices adjust before quantities: import bills rise immediately in domestic currency while export volumes take time to respond, so the balance dips before recovering. The shape of the resulting path gives the effect its name.

questions.stem: Human capital refers to:
choices: The number of workers in an economy
The skills, education, and health embodied in the workforce
Wages paid to employees
Investment by individuals in financial assets
questions.explanation: Human capital is the productive capacity embodied in people, accumulated through education, training, and health. Growth accounting consistently finds it explains a large share of cross-country income differences that physical capital alone cannot.

questions.stem: A country with a currency board arrangement:
choices: Allows its currency to float freely
Backs its currency fully with foreign reserves at a fixed rate, sharply limiting discretionary monetary policy
Uses a foreign currency as legal tender
Adjusts its exchange rate monthly against a basket
questions.explanation: A currency board issues domestic currency only against foreign reserves at a fixed rate, which buys credibility at the cost of a lender of last resort. Hong Kong is the durable example; Argentina's convertibility regime is the cautionary one.

questions.stem: A section's caseload rose 25% and then fell 20%. Compared with the start, the caseload is now:
choices: 5% higher
Unchanged
5% lower
45% higher
questions.explanation: Starting at 100: 100 × 1.25 = 125, then 125 × 0.80 = 100. The increase and decrease happen to cancel exactly here because 0.8 is the reciprocal of 1.25 — which is not the general rule, as a 10% rise and 10% fall do not cancel.

questions.stem: Which sample is most likely to produce an unbiased estimate of average household income in a city?
choices: Interviews conducted outside a luxury shopping center
A random sample drawn from a comprehensive address list
Responses to a mailed questionnaire, of which 8% were returned
Interviews with attendees at a public budget hearing
questions.explanation: Random selection from a complete frame gives every household a known chance of inclusion. The other three each select on a characteristic correlated with income or civic engagement, and an 8% response rate leaves enormous room for nonresponse bias.

questions.stem: If a post's budget is $2.4 million and personnel costs are $1.5 million, personnel represents approximately what share?
questions.explanation: 1.5 ÷ 2.4 = 0.625, or about 63%. The 38% distractor is the complement — the share represented by everything other than personnel.

questions.stem: A regression finds that each additional year of education is associated with a 7% increase in earnings, controlling for experience. The most cautious interpretation is that:
choices: Education causes a 7% earnings increase
Education is associated with higher earnings, though unobserved traits may drive part of the relationship
Experience does not affect earnings
Everyone should pursue more education
questions.explanation: Controlling for observed variables does not eliminate unobserved ones such as ability or family background. This is precisely why economists have invested so much effort in natural experiments to isolate the causal return to schooling.

questions.stem: A visa section approves 3 of every 5 applications. Out of 850 applications, approximately how many are refused?
questions.explanation: Refusals are 2/5 of the total: 0.4 × 850 = 340. The 510 distractor is the number approved, and 425 is simply half — the trap for anyone who reads the ratio as roughly even.

questions.stem: Two posts report identical average processing times, but Post A's standard deviation is three times Post B's. This means:
choices: Post A processes more cases
Post A's processing times are far more variable, so some applicants wait much longer
Post A is more efficient
The averages must have been computed incorrectly
questions.explanation: Equal means with unequal dispersion means Post A has a wider spread of outcomes — more very fast and very slow cases. From an applicant's perspective, predictability often matters as much as the average, which is why dispersion belongs in any service report.

questions.stem: A country's exports are $45 billion and imports are $52 billion. Its trade balance is:
choices: A surplus of $7 billion
A deficit of $7 billion
A surplus of $97 billion
Balanced
questions.explanation: Exports minus imports gives 45 − 52 = −$7 billion, a deficit. Adding the two figures, as the third option does, produces total trade volume rather than the balance.

questions.stem: An index is set to 100 in the base year. If it reads 138 this year, prices have risen:
choices: 138% since the base year
38% since the base year
1.38% since the base year
Cannot be determined
questions.explanation: An index of 138 means the level is 1.38 times the base, a 38% increase. Reading the index value itself as the percentage change is the standard error and overstates the rise dramatically.

questions.stem: Of 500 surveyed, 300 support a measure, 150 oppose, and 50 are undecided. Among those with an opinion, what share support it?
questions.explanation: Excluding the undecided leaves 450 with an opinion, and 300/450 = 67%. The 60% figure uses all 500 as the denominator — the choice of denominator is exactly what makes poll results arguable.

questions.stem: A test correctly identifies 99% of cases and has a 1% false positive rate. In a population where the condition affects 1 in 10,000, a positive result means the person is:
choices: Almost certainly affected
Very probably unaffected, because false positives vastly outnumber true ones
Affected with 99% probability
Equally likely affected or not
questions.explanation: Among a million people, about 100 are affected and 99 test positive, while about 9,999 unaffected people also test positive. Fewer than 1% of positives are genuine — the same base rate reasoning that makes rare-event screening so difficult.

questions.stem: If a report's figures are given in constant 2015 dollars, this means they:
choices: Have been adjusted to remove the effect of inflation
Were collected in 2015
Include only spending that occurred in 2015
Have been converted to a foreign currency
questions.explanation: Constant-dollar figures express all years in the purchasing power of the base year, making changes comparable across time. Current-dollar figures do not, which is why the two series can tell different stories about the same spending.

questions.stem: A bar chart's vertical axis begins at 90 rather than 0, and the bars range from 92 to 97. The most likely effect is to:
choices: Understate the differences between categories
Exaggerate the apparent differences between categories
Have no effect on interpretation
Make the chart easier to read without distortion
questions.explanation: Truncating the axis magnifies small differences visually — a 5-point gap can be made to look enormous. It is sometimes defensible when small differences genuinely matter, but it always requires that the reader notice the axis.

questions.stem: Fiscal policy is distinguished from monetary policy in that fiscal policy involves:
choices: Central bank operations in government securities
Government decisions about taxation and spending
Setting reserve requirements for banks
Managing the exchange rate
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the legislature's and treasury's domain — taxes and expenditure — while monetary policy belongs to the central bank. The distinction matters institutionally because the two are usually controlled by different actors with different time horizons.

questions.stem: An automatic stabilizer is best illustrated by:
choices: A one-time stimulus payment approved by legislation
Unemployment insurance, which pays out more as the economy weakens without new legislation
A central bank rate cut during a recession
A tariff imposed to protect a struggling industry
questions.explanation: Automatic stabilizers respond to the cycle without discretionary action, cushioning downturns immediately rather than after a legislative delay. Progressive income taxes work the same way, collecting less as incomes fall.

questions.stem: The informal economy refers to:
choices: Economic activity that is unrecorded, untaxed, and outside formal regulation
Barter arrangements only
Illegal activity exclusively
The service sector
questions.explanation: The informal sector includes much legal activity — street vending, unregistered workshops, casual labor — that simply operates outside official systems. It can account for a majority of employment in low-income countries, which is why GDP figures there understate activity.

questions.stem: The 'tragedy of the commons' describes:
choices: Overexploitation of a shared resource because individual users bear only part of the cost
Government mismanagement of public land
The failure of central planning
Underinvestment in public infrastructure
questions.explanation: Each user captures the full benefit of additional use while sharing the cost, so the resource is depleted — overfishing is the standard example. Elinor Ostrom's work showed that communities often solve it through governance arrangements without either privatization or state control.

questions.stem: A country's savings rate matters for growth primarily because savings:
choices: Reduce consumption and therefore lower inflation
Finance the investment that expands productive capacity
Determine the exchange rate
Are counted directly in GDP
questions.explanation: Domestic savings fund domestic investment, or must be supplemented by foreign capital. The relationship is the core of standard growth models, though the returns to additional capital diminish as an economy becomes capital-rich.

questions.stem: Two countries with similar per capita income can differ substantially in living standards because per capita income does not capture:
choices: The distribution of income, public services, and non-market production
The size of the population
The value of exports
The rate of inflation
questions.explanation: An average conceals distribution, and national accounts miss unpaid household work and undervalue public provision of health and education. This is why composite measures such as the Human Development Index are used alongside income figures.
